graphics.settings.title: Your universe

graphics.code.title: Your experiment is real code.
graphics.code.text: See the scene and camera model below. Download the full HTML with its renderer: it opens in a browser and works without internet.
graphics.download.ready: Your scene is ready. Open the downloaded HTML in a browser.
graphics.download.failed: Could not build the file. Please try downloading again.
graphics.concept.space.text: Each orbit has its own plane. Rotating the camera changes the projection and reveals the depth.
graphics.concept.light.text: Lighting reveals the shape of each sphere. Surface patterns, transparent rings and stars form a scene with depth.
graphics.concept.motion.text: Time and orbit radius determine each planet’s position. Change the speed or pause the scene to study its details.
graphics.workshop.intro: Study the Nexus system or start with an empty scene. Build your model, write JavaScript, run the result and save your project to continue later.
graphics.workshop.start.title: Study the example. Build your own.
graphics.workshop.template.nexus.text: 10 categories and 52 courses. The same orbits, spheres and renderer as the home page.
graphics.workshop.template.orbit.text: A core and a planet: build motion in space.
graphics.workshop.template.system.text: A starting model to extend with your code.
graphics.workshop.template.blank.text: A blank canvas and scene(). Everything else is yours.
graphics.workshop.settings.note: These parameters are available through settings. Build the scene in the editor; controls affect the properties your code uses.
graphics.workshop.code.title: Your scene starts with your code.
graphics.workshop.code.text: Edit scene.js and run your changes. scene(time, settings) returns bodies and orbits. Ctrl+Enter runs the code; Ctrl+S saves the project.
graphics.workshop.chapter.data.text: In the Nexus example, categories become planets and courses become moons. The catalog and orbit parameters come from our system. Edit groups, names and colors.
graphics.workshop.chapter.bodies.text: A body uses position, radius and color. terrain chooses the surface pattern; spin and axialTilt define rotation. sun gives the core an emissive surface; ringed adds rings.
graphics.workshop.chapter.orbits.text: Nexus.orbit(angle, radius, tilt, node) computes a 3D position. tilt inclines the plane and node rotates it. Code uses radians for inclination.
graphics.workshop.chapter.moons.text: Compute a moon’s local orbit, then add its planet’s position. The moon travels with the planet while continuing to orbit it.
graphics.workshop.chapter.time.text: time is scene time in seconds. Use phase + time * speed for an angle; different speeds produce different periods. Pause stops time while keeping the camera interactive.
graphics.workshop.chapter.missing: This template does not have this block yet; add it yourself.
graphics.workshop.engine.text: This is the home system’s actual renderer: WebGL surface and lighting shaders, perspective projection, orbits and stars. Canvas handles WebGL fallback. HTML includes this renderer, the camera and your scene.js.
graphics.workshop.engine.failed: Could not load the renderer source.
graphics.workshop.save.title: Come back and keep building.
graphics.workshop.save.text: Source and settings are saved in My Projects on this device. Drafts recover after reload. JSON transfers an editable project; HTML contains the scene you have run.
